title: kernel-quant-bench-notes-int8-awq-fp8-march2026
summary: Exploratory notes capturing a small matrix of runs comparing INT8 GPTQ/AWQ, FP8 (experimental runtime path), and kernel choices (fused matmul, attention blocking, vectorized GEMM) across two medium-size LLMs. Primary goal: surface clear, actionable microprofiling signals that inform kernel selection heuristics for the serving runtime and whether AWQ gives a reasonable latency/quality win over GPTQ on our hardware.
goals: 1) Identify where kernel-level choices change token latency under different quant formats. 2) Measure downstream quality delta (perplexity / CMP) for GPTQ vs AWQ vs FP8 on short/long context. 3) Produce a short list of runtime heuristics for model/sequence-length to kernel mapping.
experimental_setup:
- Machines: p4d-like instance (8xA100 80GB) for multi-GPU validation; single-GPU test bench: A100-40GB (dev rack).
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.2, cuBLAS/cutlass patches from runtime-kernel-experiments branch.
- Runtime build: local dev build with kernel flags: --enable-fused-matmul --attn-block=32/64/128 where noted.
- Models: piccolo-marco-3b (decoder-only 3B), concord-7b (7B).
- Workloads: 1) interactive short prompt (max_tokens=64, prompt len 32), 2) long-context generation (prompt len 512, max_tokens 256).
- Eval data: 200 prompts sampled from prod prompt set (anonymized) and 100 deterministic eval prompts for perplexity/quality.
hardware_config: single-GPU bench: A100-40GB, PCIe Gen4, 80GB host RAM, 1x NVMe scratch. Multi-GPU: DGX-like with NVLink. Note: observed power-limited behavior on A100-40 when running fused kernels concurrently in multi-worker test (see detailed_notes).
models_tested:
- piccolo-marco-3b: baseline FP16 (reference), GPTQ-8, AWQ-8 (per-channel, outlier handling), FP8-experimental
- concord-7b: same matrix but fewer AWQ variants due to conversion time limits
quant_methods: GPTQ-8 (standard per-channel scale + zero point), AWQ-8 (adaptive weight quantization with asymmetric outlier handling), FP8 (E4M3 style simulated path in runtime), INT8-symmetric baseline for kernel perf baseline
kernel_variants:
- fused-matmul (our custom fused GEMM + bias + activation)
- vector-gemm (cutlass-based vectorized GEMM)
- blocked-attn (attention tiled with KV cache reuse, block sizes 32/64/128)
- fallback-cuBLAS (baseline)
Note: fused-matmul shows different memory access patterns with AWQ-packed weights.
benchmark_commands:
- ./run_inference_bench --model=piccolo-marco-3b --quant=gptq8 --kernel=fused-matmul --prompt-set=short-prompts --batch=1 --seq=96 --iters=200
- ./run_inference_bench --model=concord-7b --quant=awq8 --kernel=vector-gemm --prompt-set=long-prompts --batch=1 --seq=768 --iters=50
- profiler: nvprof --metrics gld_throughput,gst_throughput,achieved_occupancy -- ./run_inference_bench ...
- wallclock measurement script: tools/measure_latency.sh capturing p50/p95/p99 and token/sec, and per-token kernel breakdown via trace sampling
metrics_captured:
- latency: p50, p90, p95, p99 per-token and end-to-end request
- throughput: tokens/sec steady-state
- memory: peak GPU RAM, allocator fragmentation
- quality: perplexity on eval set, exact-match on 10 QA prompts, BLEU/ROUGE on generated continuations
- kernel-level: time spent in GEMM, attention, KV-copy, kernel-launch overhead, cache misses (L2), global memory load throughput
- stability: OOM occurrences, numerical anomalies recorded (NaN/Inf)
high_level_results:
- AWQ-8 + fused-matmul reduced per-token latency by ~12-18% vs GPTQ-8 + cuBLAS on short prompts for piccolo-3b with no measurable perplexity degradation on our 100-eval prompts.
- On long-context workloads, blocked-attn with block=64 produced best tradeoff: AWQ+blocked-attn improved latency by 20% vs baseline but increased L2 pressure; GPTQ had marginally better perplexity (~0.6% lower) on 512+ token contexts in concord-7b.
- FP8 path shows potential for latency parity with AWQ but produced sporadic small numeric regressions in corner cases (rare NaN in one prompt out of 200).
- Fused matmul is very sensitive to weight packing layout; AWQ packed weights (4-bit-aligned packing used by our converter) improved memory throughput but forced additional unpacking work for vector-gemm kernels, sometimes negating wins.
detailed_notes:
- Profiling snapshot (piccolo, short prompts, AWQ+fused): GEMM 46% | Attention 28% | KV-copy 8% | Kernel-launch 4% | Other 14%.
- Observed that fused-matmul reduces kernel-launch overhead but increases register pressure; on A100-40 some runs saw lower achieved occupancy when block size >64.
- AWQ conversion pipeline: converter v0.9 produces slightly different scale factors than research branch; need to reconcile with quant-stats tool (tool reported 4% more outlier bins than expected).
- FP8 path currently uses simulated quant within FP16 kernels (no custom kernels yet) — explains why latency is similar but reliability differs.
- Memory fragmentation: AWQ packed weight blobs are smaller leading to lower peak memory, but packing alignment forced additional padding when using vector-gemm causing 6-8% extra allocation in that path.
- Strange multi-GPU note: when two workers on same node run fused-matmul AWQ concurrently, we hit PCIe saturation earlier than with cuBLAS path — likely due to packing/unpacking device-host ops hitting PCIe in our implementation. Need to validate if NVLink mitigates.
interpretation:
- AWQ appears promising as a default quant path for short-interactive workloads if fused kernels are available and properly optimized for AWQ packing.
- For long-context, GPTQ still slightly better for quality-sensitive workloads; runtime should offer per-model config to prefer GPTQ for pre-known eval-critical models.
- FP8 is promising but unstable; flag as experimental and gate behind numeric checks.
- Kernel heuristics: prefer fused-matmul + AWQ for seq < 256 and batch <=1; prefer blocked-attn with vector-gemm for seq >=512; fallback to cuBLAS/GEMM for models with irregular packing or when packing causes excessive padding.

open_questions:
- Why does AWQ-packed fused kernel reduce occupancy on A100-40 at block sizes >64? Is it register pressure or shared memory footprint?
- Can we implement an in-place unpack that avoids host-device transfers for vector-gemm paths?
- How representative are the 200 anonymized prompts of real prod distribution for long-context? Need sampling justification.
- Do model converters need extra calibration for FP8 to avoid rare NaNs?
